clue.text: Plant carrier packed by former Antiques Roadshow host

indicators.note: something packed by another is stuffed inside it, so the carrier goes within the host's name

parts.note: Michael Aspel presented the BBC's Antiques Roadshow for many years
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A pot plant is smuggled in the luggage of a retired television presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Antiques Roadshow is a long-running BBC programme where experts value the public's heirlooms; Michael Aspel once hosted it.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Pretend to like flightless birds climbing

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: emus are large Australian birds that cannot fly

explanation.surface: Someone affects a fondness for ostrich-like birds that are clambering upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' signals reading upwards; 'to like' is easily misread as part of the definition, but it supplies AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend an air or manner is to adopt or feign it.

clue.text: I'm suspicious about one on a charge coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the whole run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
I is the Roman numeral for one
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: A suspect frets that someone is about to be charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole string CAIONARAP upwards. The definition is the answer speaking: someone who says 'I'm suspicious' of everything is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given to irrational mistrust of everyone describes themselves as suspicious.

clue.text: Opening price means loss of alternatives

parts.note: an opening is a chance or opportunity
a cost is the price paid

explanation.surface: An economics lesson on what a starting price implies for lost choices.
explanation.definitionFit: The economists' term names the value of the best alternative forgone when making a choice.

clue.text: Mordred uplifted over Wednesday's solution having been edited

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means the setter's pronoun is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter's pseudonym stands for the setter, so ME
over means finished or ended

explanation.surface: The setter admits that an earlier puzzle's answer has had to be corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns ME into EM. 'Wednesday's solution' is surface colour, a nod to a correction of an earlier puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Emended text has been corrected and revised, as an editor would do.

clue.text: Punctuation mark editor discouraged

parts.note: a dash is a mark of punctuation

explanation.surface: An editor is disheartened by a misused punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes that are dashed have been crushed, leaving one disheartened.

clue.text: He has growing concern 0 P about liturgical sutra

indicators.note: about means moving around, so these letters are set about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man worries about a piece of religious scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LITURGICALSUTRA. 'growing concern' puns on business jargon: his concern is growing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer or agronomist's business is cultivation, so his trade is literally a growing concern.

clue.text: Scots girl not for hair B A A dye

parts.note: hen is a Scottish form of address to a woman or girl
na is Scots for not

explanation.surface: A Scottish lass refuses to colour her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The reddish plant extract is traditionally used to colour hair.

clue.text: Ruins of French ancient city originally Savoyard

parts.note: des is a French word for of the (plural)
Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A traveller describes the ruins of an old city in the French region of Savoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck something is to destroy it, so ruins is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Arrange considerable increase

parts.note: tidy means considerable, as in a tidy sum
up means an increase, as in a rise or upturn

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a large rise in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to straighten or neaten them.

clue.text: Drinks overturned in rage

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the drinks word is read backwards

parts.note: ports are fortified wines

explanation.surface: Glasses are knocked over in a fit of anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns PORTS into STROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a British colloquial word for a sulky fit of bad temper.

clue.text: They may be streaming out

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in place, so the letters of streaming are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crowds of people are pouring out of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges STREAMING, and the whole clue also describes people leaving their homeland in a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: People leaving their country to settle abroad may leave in great numbers, flowing outwards.

clue.text: Potentially find Mary a loyal servant

indicators.note: potentially means these letters could become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that one might discover a faithful maid named Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges FINDMARYA. The name comes from Crusoe's companion in Defoe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means a devoted personal assistant, after Robinson Crusoe's faithful companion.

clue.text: Primarily cash has appeal — it's really easy, e.g…

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Money is attractive because it makes life simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is one example: an easy chair is a kind of seat, and the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy is a type of seat, the armchair, so the word stands as an example.

clue.text: … to convert two pounds I split

indicators.note: split means broken apart, so the pounds pair is opened up for the letter I

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound and quid is slang for a pound sterling
L is the abbreviation for a pound and quid is slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A trader splits the cash he exchanges, two pounds each.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the previous clue: assets that are 'really easy ... to convert' into cash are liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid assets are those readily turned into cash, so the word describes ease of conversion.

clue.text: Help out rebuilding gym with stoicism

indicators.note: out means awry or not in place, so the first word's letters are scrambled

parts.note: the four letters of the word help are rearranged

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting together again in a new form, so the gym letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters of gym are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand refitting a gymnasium with calm endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns HELP into PHLE and 'rebuilding' turns GYM into GMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm is stolid calmness, so being full of it means showing unflappable composure.

clue.text: Letter a saint composed in support of a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue support sits underneath, so the anagram goes below the girl

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A holy man writes a letter on behalf of a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns A SAINT into ATIANS, placed under GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's epistle to the people of Galatia is a New Testament letter.

clue.text: In I grope, getting into something more comfortable

indicators.note: getting into suggests working the letters into a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fumbling suitor gropes about while she slips into nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' rearranges the eight letters of IN I GROPE. 'Slip into something more comfortable' is the classic seductive line.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dressing gown or negligee is what one changes into to relax.

clue.text: Cut charming first impression

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, and the following word first tells us where: the opening letter goes

parts.note: fetching means attractive or charming

explanation.surface: A cut-glass charm makes a good first impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut ... first' removes the first letter of FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: A print taken from an engraved plate is a kind of impression.

clue.text: Manoeuvre piece for end of match

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the piece replaces the final letter of the match

parts.note: a game is a match
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A chess player plans a move with one piece for the endgame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for end of' swaps the E at the end of GAME for BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening ploy or calculated move to gain advantage is a stratagem or manoeuvre.

clue.text: I'd abandoned sordid hovel ultimately in fit of temper

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the letters I and D are dropped

parts.note: squalid means sordid and filthy

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone flew into a rage after leaving a filthy shack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes ID from SQUALID to leave SQUAL; 'ultimately' adds the L ending hovel.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent outburst, of weather or of anger.

clue.text: A strain original

indicators.note: original suggests something new and unprecedented, so these letters are made over into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A tune that is quite unlike anything heard before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' rearranges ASTRAIN. As a whole the clue praises the crooner: a voice, or strain of melody, that was entirely his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank the crooner was a one-off performer whose singing style was copied by many but modelled on few.

clue.text: A girl with ashes initially eponymous

definitions.text: A girl with ashes initially eponymous

parts.note: an is the form of the indefinite article a before a vowel
gel is an upper-class pronunciation of girl

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word ashes

explanation.surface: A young woman with cinders gives her name to something.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue points to Frank McCourt's memoir Angela's Ashes, named after his mother: she is the eponymous girl with ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: The memoir's title takes this woman's first name, so she is the one it is named after.

clue.text: Dizzy Gillespie initially has old woman's head going

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the jazzman's surname
head going means the first letter is lost from the old woman

parts.note: biddy is a slightly disparaging word for an old woman

explanation.surface: The jazz trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie watches an old lady lose her bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: Dizzy Gillespie was a jazz trumpeter, so 'Dizzy' reads as a name; it is the definition. 'head going' turns BIDDY into IDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy means lightheaded or dizzy.

clue.text: Decline a little of the hard stuff, drinking nothing

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so nothing goes inside the small measure

parts.words: a little of the hard stuff
parts.note: a drop is a small measure of spirits
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back on spirits and drinks nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or decline, as a flower or spirits do.

clue.text: Island that's at sea by America alongside Eastern bank of Hudson

definitions.text: Island that's at sea by America alongside Eastern bank of Hudson

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word that, the 's being a link

indicators.note: in an across clue the eastern side of a word is its right-hand end, so its last letter

explanation.surface: A description of an island by the sea in America, beside a river's eastern shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns THAT into HATT. As a whole the clue describes the island: it lies on the east bank of the Hudson.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's central borough is an island bounded on its west by the Hudson River.

clue.text: Medic who might quote: 'Lend me your ears'

definitions.text: Medic who might quote: 'Lend me your ears'

parts.words: Medic who might quote: 'Lend me your ears'
parts.note: Mark Antony's line from Julius Caesar is reimagined as a request from an ear specialist

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who specialises in the ear would want patients to offer theirs for examination.

clue.text: Angry statement by taxman …

definitions.meaning: a tax assessor declaring how he values property might say '...'

explanation.surface: A taxpayer is furious at what the revenue officer says.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious, and as two words it is a rating official's declaration.

clue.text: … about state finance's final estimation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to put is to state, as in put it plainly

indicators.note: final points to the last letter of the word finance

explanation.surface: Thoughts on the state of public finances and their final assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is reputation, the estimation in which one is held.

clue.text: Carnivorous insect is on a bit of a log

parts.note: the praying mantis is a predatory insect
is shortens to 's, giving S

explanation.surface: A predatory insect sits on a piece of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' looks like timber, but it is short for logarithm.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal part of a logarithm is called by this mathematical term.
